calibration.rollingRecord: The 19:30 COT endday report called range with a bullish tilt at 38/40/22 and HELD both books into the gap, and holding was right. Its reduce at 63,040 did NOT fire - the lowest print since the handover was 63,351.8, leaving 311.8 points of clearance - and the 62,050 invalidation was never approached. Spot rose from 63,320.1 to 63,639.4, +0.50%, so the 0.00255524 BTC core gained about 0.82 USDT of mark value for doing nothing. Where endday was WRONG is in its directional emphasis: it wrote that 'a flush is the likelier first move, a squeeze is the bigger one' and priced the immediate path as down toward 63,070. The flush never came. Price bottomed 281 points above that target within an hour of the handover and then ran 888 points the other way to 64,240.3. Two lessons carry forward. First, it was right about WHERE the map pointed (up, toward the big pool) and wrong about the SEQUENCE, which is an argument for weighting the magnet more and the fast-oscillator pessimism less. Second, its add trigger at 62,150 was set on the assumption of a flush that did not arrive, which is exactly how a desk ends up watching a move it correctly identified - and it is the specific error this session is correcting by taking a small tranche rather than waiting for a level the market may never revisit.
